ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p392/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p392/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p392/r4.claim: The dual command to descend addresses Adam and Eve together; all together describes their joint descent, not the presence of Satan and the serpent.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p392/r4.anchor: ولا يدل قوله جميعا أن إبليس والحية يهبطان معهما لأن جميعا حال من ضمير الاثنين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p392/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p392/r5.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p392/r5.claim: Ibn Atiyya says Satan and the serpent descend with Adam and Eve and that hostility between them and their descendants continues to the end of time.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p392/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: ثم أخبرهما بقوله جميعا أن إبليس والحية مهبطان معهما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p392/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p392/r6.speaker: قول أول
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p392/r6.claim: One reading identifies the hostile groups as Iblis and his descendants opposed to Adam and his descendants.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p392/r6.anchor: قيل: يريد إبليس وبنيه وآدم وبنيه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p392/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p392/r7.speaker: قول ثان
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p392/r7.claim: Another reading takes the hostility as between Adam and his descendants, owing to divergent religions and opinions.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p392/r7.anchor: وقيل: أراد آدم وذريته، فالعداوة واقعة بينهم والبغضاء لاختلاف الأديان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p392/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p392/r8.speaker: أبو مسلم الأصبهاني
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p392/r8.claim: Abu Muslim says the dual address refers to Adam and Satan as two species, each encompassing many descendants, which explains the later plural address.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p392/r8.anchor: وقال أبو مسلم الأصبهاني: الخطاب لآدم عليه السلام ولكونهما جنسين صح قوله اهبطا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p392/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p392/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p392/r9.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says Adam and Eve stand for humanity because all people descend from them, explaining why they are addressed with a plural verb.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p392/r9.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: لما كان آدم وحواء عليهما السلام أصلي البشر والسببين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p392/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p392/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p392/r10.claim: The promised guidance means God’s law; following the Qur’an protects from worldly error and misery in the afterlife, while one report specifies protection from bad reckoning.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p392/r10.anchor: وهدى شريعة الله. وعن ابن عباس ضمن الله لمن اتبع القرآن أن لا يضل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p392/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p392/r11.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p392/r11.claim: Al-Razi defines guidance as following evidence through both inference and practice; it guarantees no afterlife error or misery because God guides the follower to Paradise.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p392/r11.anchor: وقال أبو عبد الله الرازي: وهذه الآية تدل على أن المراد بالهدى الذي ذكره الله تعالى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p392/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p392/r12.speaker: قول آخر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p392/r12.claim: Another view places the promise in this world; the response says it excludes religious error and hardship caused by religion, not troubles from other causes.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p392/r12.anchor: وقيل فلا يضل ولا يشقى في الدنيا. فإن قيل: المنعم بهدى الله قد يلحقه الشقاء

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p79/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p79/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p79/r3.claim: The earlier discussions explain the wisdom of Adam’s earthly trial against Satan; the address is to Adam and Satan as two groups, not Adam and Eve.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p79/r3.anchor: the address is towards Adam (sws) and Satan in the capacity of two groups

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p79/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p79/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p79/r4.claim: The groups must regard Satan as their enemy to regain Paradise; Islahi rejects reading the dual as Adam and Eve because the plural parallel, jamīʿan, and their natural love make enmity implausible.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p79/r4.anchor: the natural relationship between Adam (sws) and Eve is not of enmity: it is of love

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p80/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p80/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p80/r1.claim: God gave Adam and his descendants revelation alongside nature and intellect as a weapon for combating Satan.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p80/r1.anchor: This actually is the weapon which God had blessed Adam (sws) and his progeny with.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p80/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p80/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p80/r2.claim: God's Book is the sole protection from Satan's attacks; without it people remain vulnerable to devils among jinn and humankind.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p80/r2.anchor: the sole means to remain secure from the onslaughts of Satan in this world is the Book of God

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p80/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p80/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p80/r3.claim: Adam was a prophet sent to counter Satan, so God must have revealed a sharīʿah suited to his circumstances; Islahi refers to directives under Abel and Cain.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p80/r3.anchor: Adam (sws) was a prophet. He has been sent in this world to counter the onslaughts of Satan for which God’s guidance for both Adam (sws) and his progeny is essential

STUDYQURAN:7:11/r21.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r21.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r21.claim: Iblis’s command to get down from the Garden also appears in 2:36 and 20:123; verse 24 gives Adam and his wife a similar command.
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r21.anchor: The command to Iblīs, Get down from it—that is, leave the Garden—is also found in 2:36 and 20:123

STUDYQURAN:7:11/r78.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r78.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r78.claim: The command to descend is widely taken to address Adam, Eve and their descendants, as well as Iblis.
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r78.anchor: is widely considered to be addressed to Adam and Eve and their future progeny as well as to Iblīs, or Satan (Ṭ).

ASAD-NOTES:20:122/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:122/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:122/r2.claim: After the descent from innocence and the onset of mutual enmity, whoever follows God's guidance will neither stray nor be unhappy.
ASAD-NOTES:20:122/r2.anchor: there shall most certainly come unto you guidance from Me: and he who follows My guidance will not go astray

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p20#7/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p20#7/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p20#7/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says whoever reads the Qur’an and follows its teachings will be guided from error in this life and protected from the reckoning on Judgment Day.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p20#7/r1.anchor: عن عطاء بن السايب قال قال ابن عباس من قرأ القرآن فاتبع ما فيه هداه الله من الظلالة في الدنيا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p275#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p275#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p275#3/r1.claim: The statement answers an implied question about what God commanded Adam after the preceding account.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p275#3/r1.anchor: استئناف مبني على سؤال نشأ من الأخبار بأنه تعالى عامله

ALUSI-FULL:v16p275#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p275#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p275#3/r2.claim: The command tells Adam and his wife to descend together from the garden to earth.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p275#3/r2.anchor: أي انزلا من الجنة إلى الأرض مجتمعين

ALUSI-FULL:v16p275#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p275#3/r3.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p275#3/r3.claim: Some take the dual address to be Adam and Iblis, since Iblis entered the garden to whisper after being expelled and declared accursed.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p275#3/r3.anchor: وقيل : الخطاب له عليه السلام ولابليس عليه اللعنة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p275#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p275#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p275#3/r4.claim: On the Adam-and-wife reading, enmity is between their descendants, since the two are ancestors from whom the children arise; the clause is circumstantial.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p275#3/r4.anchor: لما أنهما أصل الذرية ومنشأ الأولاد فالتعادي في الحقيقة بين أولادهما

ALUSI-FULL:v16p275#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p275#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p275#3/r5.claim: On the first reading, the enmity clause functions as a circumstantial clause describing their state as they descend.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p275#3/r5.anchor: والجملة في موضع الحال أي متعادين في أمر المعاش وشهوات الأنفس

ALUSI-FULL:v16p275#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p275#3/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p275#3/r6.claim: If the addressees are Adam and Iblis, their own enmity and enmity between their descendants are evident.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p275#3/r6.anchor: وعلى الثاني ظاهر لظهور العداوة بين آدم عليه السلام وإبليس

ALUSI-FULL:v16p275#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p275#3/r7.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p275#3/r7.claim: Some take the pronoun to encompass Adam and his descendants, and Iblis and his descendants.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p275#3/r7.anchor: ومن هنا قيل : الضمير لآدم وذريته وابليس وذريته

ALUSI-FULL:v16p275#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p275#3/r8.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p275#3/r8.claim: A further proposal includes Adam, Iblis, the serpent, and their descendants; al-Alusi says the first interpretation is relied upon.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p275#3/r8.anchor: وزعم بعضهم أن لآدم وإبليس والحية والمعول عليه الأول

ALUSI-FULL:v16p275#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p275#3/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p275#3/r9.claim: The guidance is a prophet sent to the people and a book revealed to them.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p275#3/r9.anchor: أي نبي أرسله إليكم وكتاب أنزله عليكم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p275#3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p275#3/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p275#3/r10.claim: The explicit noun instead of a pronoun, attached to God, honors the guidance and intensifies the duty to follow it.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p275#3/r10.anchor: وضع الظاهر موضع المضمر مع الإضافة إلى ضميره تعالى لتشريفه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p275#3/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p275#3/r11.speaker: أبو الطفيل
ALUSI-FULL:v16p275#3/r11.claim: Al-Tabarani and others report from Abu al-Tufayl that the Prophet recited the clause with hudan indefinite, explaining that its follower does not stray in this life or suffer in the next; no grading is stated.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p275#3/r11.anchor: وأخرج الطبراني وغيره عن أبي الطفيل أن النبي ( صلى الله عليه وسلم ) قرأ

ALUSI-FULL:v16p275#3/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p275#3/r12.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p275#3/r12.claim: Some identify guidance specifically as the Qur’an; Ibn Abbas said God protects its follower from worldly error and afterlife misery, then recited the verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p275#3/r12.anchor: وفسر بعضهم الهدى بالقرآن لما أخرج ابن أبي شيبة وعبد بن حميد

ALUSI-FULL:v16p275#3/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p275#3/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v16p275#3/r13.claim: Ibn Abbas is also reported in a Prophetic report: whoever follows God’s Book, God guides him from error in this life and protects him from evil reckoning on Judgment Day; no grading is stated.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p275#3/r13.anchor: وأخرج جماعة عنه مرفوعا إلى رسول الله ( صلى الله عليه وسلم ) بلفظ

ALUSI-FULL:v16p276/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276/r1.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276/r1.claim: Some favor taking guidance as the Qur’an because the next verse says “whoever turns away from My remembrance,” and the following account refers to God’s signs.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276/r1.anchor: ورجح على العموم بقيام القرينة عليه وهو قوله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p276/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276/r2.claim: Al-Alusi prefers the general meaning: dhikr can mean the Qur’an or any divine scripture, and signs can mean proofs generally.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276/r2.anchor: والمختار العموم أن يقول : الذكر يقع على القرآن وعلى سائر الكتب

ALUSI-FULL:v16p276/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276/r4.claim: The report specifies the most honored instances encompassed by the general promise, highlighting their importance.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276/r4.anchor: وما في الخبر من باب التنصيص على حكم أشرف الأفراد المدلول عليه بالعموم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p276/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276/r5.claim: The report’s interpretation—no error in this world and no suffering in the hereafter—is supported by transmitted reports.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276/r5.anchor: بقولنا في الدنيا ( ولا يشقى ) بقولنا في الآخرة هو الذي يقتضيه الخبر

ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r1.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r1.claim: Another reading reverses the domains: the guided person will not lose the way to Paradise in the hereafter or tire in securing livelihood in this world.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r1.anchor: وجوز بعضهم العكس أي فلا يضل طريق الجنة في الآخرة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r2.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r2.claim: On that reading, not straying in the hereafter answers the warning about resurrection blind, while not suffering in this life answers the constricted livelihood.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r2.anchor: وجعل الأول في مقابلة ( ونحشره يوم القيامة أعمى ) والثاني في مقابلة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r3.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r3.claim: The reversed order reflects the guided people’s focus on the afterlife, unlike those whose attention is confined to worldly life.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r3.anchor: وتقديم حال الآخرة على حال الدنيا في المهتدين لأن مطمح نظرهم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r4.claim: Al-Alusi says reports support the first, worldly-error/afterlife-suffering interpretation; the reversed reading is attractive but somewhat strained.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r4.anchor: ولا يخفى أن الذي نطقت به الآثار هو الأول وذكر بعضهم أنه المتبادر

ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r5.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r5.claim: The Imam allows both consequences in the afterlife, or both in worldly life; on the latter reading there is no religious error or hardship caused by religion, though other hardship may occur.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r5.anchor: وجوز الإمام كون الأمرين في الآخرة وكونهما في الدنيا وذكر أن المراد

ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r6.claim: Al-Alusi says the interpretation supported by the reports remains the one to rely on.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p300#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p300#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p300#2/r2.claim: The guidance sent by God means the Scripture and the Messenger.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p300#2/r2.anchor: فمن اتبع هداي} يعني الكتاب والرسول، {فلا يضل ولا يشقى}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p300#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p300#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p300#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, through Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, says whoever reads the Qur’an and follows it is guided from error in this life and protected from an evil reckoning at the Resurrection.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p300#2/r3.anchor: روى سعيد بن جبر عن ابن عباس قال: من قرأ القرآن واتبع ما فيه هداه الله في الدنيا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p300#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p300#2/r4.speaker: الشعبي عن ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p300#2/r4.claim: Al-Shaʿbī reports Ibn ʿAbbās saying that God protects Qur’an followers from worldly error and misery in the afterlife.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p300#2/r4.anchor: وقال الشعبي عن ابن عباس: أجار الله تعالى تابع القرآن من أن يضل في الدنيا ويشقى

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:123/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:123/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:123/r1.claim: The dual is addressed either to Adam and Eve or to Adam and Iblis; as progenitors, Adam and Eve can be addressed in language encompassing their descendants.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:123/r1.anchor: الخطاب لآدم وحواء، أو له ولإبليس ولما كانا أصلي الذرية

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:123/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:123/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:123/r2.claim: Hostility may arise from the contest and conflict of livelihood among people, or from each kind's condition being disrupted through the other; the following favors the first.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:123/r2.anchor: لأمر المعاش كما عليه الناس من التجاذب والتحارب، أو لاختلال حال كل من النوعين

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:123/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:123/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:123/r3.claim: The guidance from God is a revealed book and a messenger.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:123/r3.anchor: كتاب ورسول. { فمن اتبع هداي فلا يضل } في الدنيا. { ولا يشقى } في الآخرة.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:123/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:123/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:123/r4.claim: Whoever follows God's guidance will not go astray in this world or suffer in the next.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:123/r4.anchor: كتاب ورسول. { فمن اتبع هداي فلا يضل } في الدنيا. { ولا يشقى } في الآخرة.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p53/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p53/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p53/r1.claim: The descent answers the listener's curiosity after Adam's wife and Iblis were mentioned without the rest of their story; the holy royal abode cannot contain such disobedience, though God had prepared Adam for it through election.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p53/r1.anchor: لم تسكن عن تشوفها إلى سماع بقية الخبر

BIQAI-FULL:v5p53/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p53/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p53/r2.claim: The two parties addressed are Adam and those who follow him, together with Iblis.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p53/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p53/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p53/r3.claim: Enmity between the camps stirs resolve after forgetfulness and weakened determination: the jinn mislead humans, humans guard against them with charms and incantations, and members of each camp also oppose one another.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p53/r3.anchor: حرك العزم بعث الهم بإيقاع العداوة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p53/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p53/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p53/r4.claim: The consequence of enmity is that no one can guard against an enemy except through God; His guidance, conveyed through the Book and an intellectually supported Messenger, is the only protection.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p53/r4.anchor: لا قدرة لأحد منكم على التحرز من عدوه إلا بي ولا حرز لكم من قبلي إلا اتباع أمري

BIQAI-FULL:v5p53/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p53/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p53/r5.claim: The morphology of ittabaʿa (form VIII) conveys effortful, complete following, prompted by the great importance of the guidance.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p53/r5.anchor: التي فيها تكلف وتتميم للتبع الناشىء عن شدة الاهتمام

BIQAI-FULL:v5p53/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p53/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p53/r6.claim: The follower of God's guidance will not stray from the right path in either life or suffer in any undertaking in either life.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p53/r6.anchor: عن طريق السداد في الدنيا ولا في الآخرة أصلا

BIQAI-FULL:v5p53/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p53/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p53/r7.claim: Since misery is the penalty for error, denying misery also denies fear and grief, making this promise stronger than the one in al-Baqara; this context urges fearful striving against enmity and neglect.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p53/r7.anchor: فإن الشقاء عقاب الضلال , ويلزم من نفيه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p53/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p53/r8.speaker: الرازي
BIQAI-FULL:v5p53/r8.claim: Al-Razi in al-Lawami defines misery as the servant's separation from God and happiness as reaching Him.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p53/r8.anchor: قال الرازي في اللوامع : والشقاء : فراق العبد

BIQAI-FULL:v5p53/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p53/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
BIQAI-FULL:v5p53/r9.claim: Al-Asbahani reports Ibn Abbas saying that God guarantees the Qur'an's follower will not stray in this world or be miserable in the next.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p53/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما

DURR-FULL:v5p606/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p606/r2.speaker: وهب بن منبه
DURR-FULL:v5p606/r2.claim: Wahb says God cursed the snake for carrying Iblis: its legs drew into its belly, it would eat only earth, and humans and snakes became mutual enemies, with people ordered to split its head when encountered.
DURR-FULL:v5p606/r2.anchor: وقال للحية: أنت التي دخل الملعون في جوفك حتى غر عبدي أنت ملعونة لعنة تتحول قوائمك في بطنك ولا يكون لك رزق إلا التراب

DURR-FULL:v5p606/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p606/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p606/r6.claim: Abu al-Tufayl reports that the Prophet recited the phrase “whoever follows My guidance.”
DURR-FULL:v5p606/r6.anchor: عن أبي الطفيل أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قرأ: {فمن اتبع هداي}

DURR-FULL:v5p606/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p606/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p606/r7.claim: The Prophet says whoever follows God's Book will be guided away from worldly error and protected from the bad reckoning in the Hereafter.
DURR-FULL:v5p606/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: من اتبع كتاب الله هداه الله من الضلالة في الدنيا ووقاه سوء الحساب يوم القيامة

DURR-FULL:v5p606/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p606/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p606/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas says God guarantees that Quran-followers will not go astray in this life or suffer in the next.
DURR-FULL:v5p606/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: أجار الله تابع القرآن من أن يضل في الدنيا أو يشقى في الآخرة

DURR-FULL:v5p607/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p607/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p607/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas explicates the promise: the follower of God's guidance does not go astray in this world or suffer in the Hereafter.
DURR-FULL:v5p607/r1.anchor: ثم قرأ: {فمن اتبع هداي فلا يضل ولا يشقى} قال: لا يضل في الدنيا ولا يشقى في الآخرة

BURSEVI:v5p338#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p338#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p338#2/r1.claim: After the lapse, God tells Adam and Eve to descend from the garden to earth; hubūṭ means descending.
BURSEVI:v5p338#2/r1.anchor: {قال} الله تعالى لآدم وحواء بعد صدور الزلة {اهبطا منها جميعا} أي : انزلا من الجنة إلى الأرض

BURSEVI:v5p338#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p338#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p338#2/r2.claim: The descent sounds like blame and reproach outwardly but means completion and honor inwardly.
BURSEVI:v5p338#2/r2.anchor: هذا خطاب العتاب واللوم في الصورة وخطاب التكميل والتشريف في المعنى

BURSEVI:v5p338#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p338#2/r3.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v5p338#2/r3.claim: Al-Raghib defines hubūṭ as downward movement under compulsion, like a stone falling; when used of a person it signals belittlement, unlike inzāl, used for honored things.
BURSEVI:v5p338#2/r3.anchor: قال الراغب الهبوط الانحدار على سبيل القهر كهبوط الحجر قال تعالى : {وإن منها لما يهبط من خشية الله}

BURSEVI:v5p338#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p338#2/r4.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v5p338#2/r4.claim: Al-Raghib supports the distinction by noting that the Quran, angels, and rain are sent down with the honorific inzāl, whereas hubūṭ occurs in contexts of contempt.
BURSEVI:v5p338#2/r4.anchor: بخلاف الإنزال فإن الإنزال ذكره الله في الأشياء التي نبه على شرفها كإنزال القرآن والملائكة والمطر وغير ذلك والهبوط ذكره حيث نبه على البغض

BURSEVI:v5p338#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p338#2/r5.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v5p338#2/r5.claim: Other uses of hubūṭ occur in contexts of enmity or humiliation, including the descent command to Adam’s descendants and Iblis’s expulsion.
BURSEVI:v5p338#2/r5.anchor: نحو {وقلنا اهبطوا بعضكم لبعض عدو} (البقرة : 36) وقال :

BURSEVI:v5p338#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p338#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p338#2/r6.claim: The enmity concerns descendants struggling and fighting over livelihood; the plural addresses Adam and Eve as the origin of their offspring, as in the verse about their descendants associating partners with God.
BURSEVI:v5p338#2/r6.anchor: أي : بعض أولادكم عدو لبعض في أمر المعاش كما عليه الناس من التجاذب والتحارب

BURSEVI:v5p338#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p338#2/r7.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p338#2/r7.claim: The inward reading says God placed enmity among people so that they would have no beloved but Him, as Abraham said that all are enemies except the Lord of the worlds.
BURSEVI:v5p338#2/r7.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : يشير إلى أنه جعل فيما بينهم العداوة لئلا يكون لهم حبيب إلا هو كما قال تعالى عن إبراهيم عليه السلام

BURSEVI:v5p338#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p338#2/r8.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p338#2/r8.claim: Because Adam was specially chosen, God sent him to earth with others for a test and promised guidance to his descendants.
BURSEVI:v5p338#2/r8.anchor: ولما اختص آدم منهم بالاجتباء والاصطفاء وأهبطه إلى الأرض معهم للابتلاء وعده بالاهتداء

BURSEVI:v5p338#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p338#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p338#2/r9.claim: The guidance refers to a revealed book and a messenger, addressed to the descendants of Adam and Eve.
BURSEVI:v5p338#2/r9.anchor: قال : {فإما يأتينكم} يا ذرية آدم وحواء {منى هدى} كتاب ورسول

BURSEVI:v5p338#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p338#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p338#2/r10.claim: The mīm in immā is augmentative to emphasize the condition; the nūn of emphasis after the verb works like an oath lām.
BURSEVI:v5p338#2/r10.anchor: والأصل فإن يأتينكم وما مزيدة لتأكيد معنى الشرط وما هذه مثل لام القسم في دخول النون المؤكدة معها

BURSEVI:v5p338#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p338#2/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p338#2/r11.claim: Conditional wording indicates that revelation by book and messenger is not an obligation upon God: He may guide or leave people, though the emphatic condition shows its occurrence is more likely.
BURSEVI:v5p338#2/r11.anchor: إتيان الكتاب والرسول لما لم يكن لازم التحقق والوقوع أبرز في معرض الشك وأكد حرف الشرط والفعل بالنون دلالة على رجحان جهة الوقوع

BURSEVI:v5p338#2/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p338#2/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p338#2/r12.claim: Following God’s guidance means believing the book and affirming the messenger; such a person will not stray from the straight religious path in this life or suffer punishment in the afterlife.
BURSEVI:v5p338#2/r12.anchor: أي : فمن آمن بالكتاب وصدق بالرسول

BURSEVI:v5p338#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p338#3/r5.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p338#3/r5.claim: In reality, guidance is a light God casts into prophets’ and saints’ hearts to lead them to Him; outwardly it is the leading scholars and shaykhs after the prophets and messengers.
BURSEVI:v5p338#3/r5.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" الهدى في الحقيقة نور يقذفه الله في قلوب أنبيائه وأوليائه ليهتدوا به إليه وفي الصورة العلماء السادة والمشايخ القادة

BURSEVI:v5p338#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p338#3/r6.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p338#3/r6.claim: Following guidance means submission, acceptance, and good example; the follower does not leave the path of truth or suffer deprivation and estrangement.
BURSEVI:v5p338#3/r6.anchor: {فمن اتبع هداى} بالتسليم والرضى والأسوة الحسنة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p328/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p328/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p328/r2.claim: The descent announcement answers the question raised by Adam's disobedience and deviation: what consequence followed?
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p328/r2.anchor: لأن الإخبار عن آدم بالعصيان والغواية يثير في نفس السامع سؤالا عن جزاء ذلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p328/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p328/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p328/r3.claim: The speaker is Adam's Lord, and the command addresses Adam and Iblis.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p328/r3.anchor: عائد إلى { ربه } ( طه : 121 ) من قوله { وعصى آدم ربه } والخطاب لآدم وإبليس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p328/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p328/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p328/r4.claim: The descent is a creative command: they could not leave the garden for earth without God's act of creation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p328/r4.anchor: لأنهما عاجزان عن الهبوط إلى الأرض إلا بتكوين من الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p328/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p328/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p328/r5.claim: Jamīʿan is a singular noun expressing all members of a plural set, invariant for gender and number, and accusative as a circumstantial qualifier.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p328/r5.anchor: اسم لمعنى كل أفراد ما يوصف بجميع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p328/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p328/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p328/r6.claim: The enmity clause is a second circumstantial qualifier of the descent command.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p328/r6.anchor: وجملة بعضكم لبعض عدو } حال ثانية من ضمير { اهبطا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p328/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p328/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p328/r7.claim: Adam and Iblis are commanded to descend; Eve follows her husband.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p328/r7.anchor: فالمأمور بالهبوط من الجنة آدم وإبليس وأما حواء فتبع لزوجها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p328/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p328/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p328/r8.claim: The plural address to Adam and Iblis includes their descendants, founders of humankind and the satanic kind.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p328/r8.anchor: وخوطبا بضمير الجمع لأنه أريد عداوة نسليهما ، فإنهما أصلان لنوعين نوع الإنسان ونوع الشيطان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p329/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p329/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p329/r1.claim: Descent introduces humanity to a mixed world of good and evil and realities and illusions, unlike the garden's pure world; this change was inherent in human nature.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p329/r1.anchor: إنباء بأنهم يستقبلون في هذه الدنيا سيرة غير التي كانوا عليها في الجنة لأنهم أودعوا في عالم خليط

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p329/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p329/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p329/r2.claim: The address is to Adam as the ancestor of humankind and anticipates that descendants will follow him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p329/r2.anchor: لآدم باعتبار أنه أصل لنوع الإنسان إشعارا له بأنه سيكون منه جماعة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p329/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p329/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p329/r3.claim: Iblis is excluded from this guidance command because God disclosed his enduring evil; asking him to seek guidance would be pointless, unlike addressing Abū Jahl.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p329/r3.anchor: ولا يشمل هذا الخطاب إبليس لأنه مفطور على الشر والضلال إذ قد أنبأه الله بذلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p329/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p329/r4.speaker: النبي ﷺ
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p329/r4.claim: A report transmitted by al-Dāraquṭnī says each person, including the Prophet, has a jinn companion; the Prophet's companion became Muslim through God's aid.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p329/r4.anchor: رواه الدارقطني أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p329/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p329/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p329/r5.claim: The report does not mean the Prophet invited his companion to Islam; God inspired the companion to command good.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p329/r5.anchor: فلا يقتضي أنه دعاه للإسلام ولكن الله ألهم قرينه إلى أن يأمره بالخير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p329/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p329/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p329/r6.claim: Here guidance means directing someone to good.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p329/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p329/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p329/r7.claim: God charges Adam and his descendants to follow God's messengers and divine revelation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p329/r7.anchor: وصاية الله آدم وذريته باتباع رسل الله والوحي الإلهي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p329/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p329/r8.speaker: علماء الإسلام
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p329/r8.claim: Many Muslim scholars hold that knowledge of the one God is innate in human reason or widespread across generations.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p329/r8.anchor: قال كثير من علماء الإسلام : إن معرفة الإله الواحد كائنة في العقول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p329/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p329/r9.speaker: كثير من علماء الإسلام
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p329/r9.claim: Many Muslim scholars hold that polytheists in periods without messengers are not excused from punishment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p329/r9.anchor: لم يعذر أهل الشرك في مدد الفتر التي لم تجىء فيها رسل للأمم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p330/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p330/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p330/r1.claim: The first two clauses have already been interpreted in their parallel passage in al-Baqara.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p330/r1.anchor: وقد تقدم تفسير نظير الجملتين الأولين في سورة البقرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p330/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p330/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p330/r2.claim: Following guidance from God's messengers prevents every kind of worldly misguidance; the negative construction is universal.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p330/r2.anchor: سلم من أن يعتريه شيء من ضلال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p330/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p330/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p330/r3.claim: Human-made religious systems cannot ensure freedom from error because of oversight, conflicting evidence, customs, and appeasing leaders or nations.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p330/r3.anchor: بسبب غفلات ، أو تعارض أدلة ، أو انفعال بعادات مستقرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p330/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p330/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p330/r4.claim: Socrates illustrates the limits of human wisdom: he disguised moral instruction in animal tales and, despite not deifying the gods, ordered a rooster offered to Hermes.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p330/r4.anchor: وهذا سقراط وهو سيد حكماء اليونان قد كان يتذرع لإلقاء الأمر بالمعروف في أثينا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p330/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p330/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p330/r5.claim: Messengers receive revelation from the all-knowing God, are supported and protected from appeasing whims, and are formed and steadfast for their mission.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p330/r5.anchor: الرسل الذين يتلقون الوحي من علام الغيوب الذي لا يضل ولا ينسى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p330/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p330/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p330/r6.claim: The promised freedom from wretchedness concerns the afterlife: avoiding error in this life saves one from the misery described for those who turn away in 20:124.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p330/r6.anchor: هو شقاء الآخرة لأنه إذا سلم من الضلال في الدنيا سلم من الشقاء في الآخرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p68#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p68#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p68#2/r3.claim: The command addresses Adam and Eve; “all together” indicates Iblis and the serpent descend with them and enmity persists among them and their descendants.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p68#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p68#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p68#2/r4.claim: عدو describes one, two, or many.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p68#2/r4.anchor: وعدو يوصف به الواحد والاثنان والجميع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p68#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p68#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p68#2/r5.claim: This is a conditional clause, answered by فمن اتبع هداي and what follows through the second category.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p68#2/r5.anchor: فإما يأتينكم مني هدى شرط وجوابه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p68#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p68#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p68#2/r6.claim: The guidance is a divinely prescribed summons.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p68#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p68#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p68#2/r7.claim: Those who follow God's guidance and believe will not go astray in this world or suffer in the afterlife.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p68#2/r7.anchor: وآمن به فإنه «لا يضل» في الدنيا ولا يشقى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#2/r1.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#2/r1.claim: Muqatil identifies the two commanded to descend as Adam and Iblis.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#2/r2.speaker: أبو سليمان الدمشقي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#2/r2.claim: Abu Sulayman al-Dimashqi identifies them as Adam and Eve.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#2/r2.anchor: والثاني آدم وحواء قاله أبو سليمان الدمشقي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#2/r3.claim: The mutual enmity is between Adam and his descendants, Iblis and his descendants, and the serpent; the discussion is also given at 2:36.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#2/r3.anchor: آدم وذريته وإبليس وذريته والحية أيضا وقد شرحنا هذا في البقرة 36

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#2/r4.claim: God's guidance here means His messenger and His Book.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#2/r4.anchor: فمن اتبع هداي أي رسولي وكتابي فلا يضل ولا يشقى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says whoever reads the Qur'an and follows its contents is guided from error and protected from a bad reckoning; he then recited this verse.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#2/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس من قرأ القرآن واتبع ما فيه هداه الله من الضلالة ووقاه سوء الحساب ولقد ضمن الله لمن اتبع القرآن أن لا يضل في الدنيا ولا يشقى في الآخرة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p322#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p322#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p322#2/r1.claim: God commands Adam, Eve, and Iblis all to descend from Paradise; Ibn Kathir says the matter was treated at length in al-Baqara.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p322#2/r1.anchor: يقول تعالى لآدم وحواء وإبليس: اهبطوا منها جميعا، أي: من الجنة كلكم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p322#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p322#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p322#2/r2.claim: The enemies are Adam and his descendants on one side, and Iblis and his descendants on the other.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p322#2/r2.anchor: {بعضكم لبعض عدو} قال: آدم وذريته، وإبليس وذريته

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p322#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p322#2/r3.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p322#2/r3.claim: Abu al-Aliya identifies the promised guidance as the prophets, messengers, and clear explanation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p322#2/r3.anchor: قال أبو العالية: الأنبياء والرسل والبيان

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p322#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p322#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p322#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says the follower of God's guidance does not go astray in this life or suffer in the next.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p322#2/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس: لا يضل في الدنيا، ولا يشقى في الآخرة

JISHUMI:v7p4758/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4758/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4758/r6.claim: The sentence ends after جميعا; بعضكم لبعض عدو begins a new sentence.
JISHUMI:v7p4758/r6.anchor: تم الكلام، ثم استأنف (بعضكم لبعض عدو)

JISHUMI:v7p4758/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4758/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4758/r7.claim: The م in فإما is connective and means فإن; the conditional construction takes the emphatic nūn and فلا يضل is its answer.
JISHUMI:v7p4758/r7.anchor: و (ما) في قوله: (فإما يأتينكم) صلة، والمعنى: فإن يأتينكم، وهو شرط لذلك دخلت النون

JISHUMI:v7p4758/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4758/r15.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4758/r15.claim: The dual address is to Adam and his faction, and to Iblis and his faction.
JISHUMI:v7p4758/r15.anchor: قيل: خطاب لآدم وحزبه وإبليس وحزبه

JISHUMI:v7p4758/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4758/r16.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4758/r16.claim: The descending parties are enemies to one another.

JISHUMI:v7p4758/r17.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4758/r17.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4758/r17.claim: The guidance sent by God means a messenger, scripture, and clear explanation.
JISHUMI:v7p4758/r17.anchor: فإما يأتينكم مني هدى أي: رسول وكتاب وبيان

JISHUMI:v7p4758/r18.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4758/r18.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v7p4758/r18.claim: Following the guidance means following the book and messenger; it brings no error in this world and no misery in the next.
JISHUMI:v7p4758/r18.anchor: فمن اتبع هداي يعني الكتاب والرسول فلا يضل ولا يشقى قيل: لا يضل في الدنيا ولا يشقى في الآخرة، عن ابن عباس

JISHUMI:v7p4758/r19.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4758/r19.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4758/r19.claim: God guarantees that whoever reads the Quran and acts on it will not stray in this world or be miserable in the afterlife.
JISHUMI:v7p4758/r19.anchor: ضمن الله لمن يقرأ القرآن ويعمل بما فيه ألا يضل في الدنيا ولا يشقى في الآخرة

JISHUMI:v7p4761/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4761/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4761/r8.claim: These verses show that human acts originate from human agents, contradicting the compulsion doctrine.
JISHUMI:v7p4761/r8.anchor: ويدل قوله: (فمن اتبع هداي) و(ومن أعرض عن ذكري) على أن فعل العبد حادث من جهته

JISHUMI:v7p4761/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4761/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4761/r9.claim: Guidance here means indication and explanation, not faith itself, contrary to the compulsion doctrine.
JISHUMI:v7p4761/r9.anchor: وتدل على أن الهدى الدلالة والبيان دون نفس الإيمان

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p94#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p94#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p94#2/r1.claim: Adam and Eve are humanity’s two origins and are addressed as humanity in the plural, like assigning an effect’s act to its cause.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p94#2/r1.anchor: لما كان آدم وحواء عليهما السلام أصلى البشر ، والسببين اللذين منها نشؤا وتفرعوا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p94#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p94#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p94#2/r2.claim: Guidance here means scripture and religious law.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p94#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p94#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p94#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says God guarantees that Qur’an followers will not stray in this world or suffer in the next; he recited this verse.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p94#2/r3.anchor: وعن ابن عباس : ضمن الله لمن اتبع القرآن أن لا يضل في الدنيا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p94#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p94#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p94#2/r4.claim: Hereafter misery punishes those who strayed from religion in this life; following the Book and obeying it saves from error and punishment.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p94#2/r4.anchor: أن الشقاء في الآخرة هو عقاب من ضل في الدنيا عن طريق الدين

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p430/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p430/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p430/r1.claim: Following God's guidance means acting on its contents and brings neither error in this world nor misery.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p430/r1.anchor: وعمل بما فيه { فلا يضل ولا يشقى } لا يضل في الدنيا ولا يشقى

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p430/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p430/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p430/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says God guarantees that whoever reads the Quran and acts by it will not stray in this world or suffer in the afterlife.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p430/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس : ضمن الله لمن يقرأ القرآن ويعمل بما فيه ألا يضل في الدنيا ولا يشقى في الآخرة

MUJAHID:v1p404#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p404#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MUJAHID:v1p404#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says following God's guidance means reading the Quran and following its contents; God then guides one from error and protects one from an evil reckoning.
MUJAHID:v1p404#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله عز وجل ﴿ فمن اتبع هداي فلا يضل ولا يشقى ﴾ يقول من قرأ القرآن واتبع ما فيه

MUQATIL:20:123-125/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:123-125/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:123-125/r1.claim: The two commanded to descend are Adam and Iblis.
MUQATIL:20:123-125/r1.anchor: { قال اهبطا منها جميعا } يعنى آدم وإبليس

MUQATIL:20:123-125/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:123-125/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:123-125/r2.claim: Iblis and his descendants are enemies of Adam and his descendants.
MUQATIL:20:123-125/r2.anchor: { بعضكم لبعض عدو } يقول: إبليس وذريته عدو لآدم وذريته

MUQATIL:20:123-125/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:123-125/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:123-125/r3.claim: The guidance comes through messengers bearing books that contain clarification.
MUQATIL:20:123-125/r3.anchor: يعنى رسلا معهم كتب فيها البيان

MUQATIL:20:123-125/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:123-125/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:123-125/r4.claim: Following God's guidance means following His messengers and His book.
MUQATIL:20:123-125/r4.anchor: { فمن اتبع هداي } يعنى رسلى وكتابى

MUQATIL:20:123-125/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:123-125/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:123-125/r5.claim: The follower will not go astray in this world or suffer in the next.
MUQATIL:20:123-125/r5.anchor: { فلا يضل } فى الدنيا { ولا يشقى } [آية: 123] فى الآخرة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p70#7/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p70#7/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p70#7/r1.claim: The two addressed are Adam and Eve.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p70#7/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p70#7/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p70#7/r2.claim: The enmity is among Adam’s descendants, through worldly envy and disagreement in religion.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p70#7/r2.anchor: عدو بالتحاسد فى الدنيا والاختلاف فى الدين

NASAFI-FULL:v3p70#7/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p70#7/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p70#7/r3.claim: The guidance sent by God is a revealed book and religious law.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p70#7/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p70#7/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p70#7/r4.claim: Following God’s guidance prevents worldly error and misery in the Hereafter.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p70#7/r4.anchor: ﴿ فمن اتبع هداي فلا يضل ﴾ فى الدنيا ﴿ ولا يشقى ﴾ في العقبى

NASAFI-FULL:v3p70#7/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p70#7/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
NASAFI-FULL:v3p70#7/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says God guarantees Quran followers will not stray in this life or suffer in the next.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p70#7/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما ضمن الله لمن اتبع القرأن الا يضل فى الدنيا

NASAFI-FULL:v3p70#7/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p70#7/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p70#7/r6.claim: The one who follows God’s Book, obeys its commands, and avoids its prohibitions escapes both misguidance and punishment.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p70#7/r6.anchor: فمن اتبع كتاب الله وامتثل أوامره وانتهى عن نواهية نجا من الضلال ومن عقابه

QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r1.claim: The dual command addresses Adam and Iblis, and منها means the Garden; the command to expel Iblis in 7:18 may imply an initial expulsion to a heavenly place before descent to earth.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r1.anchor: خاطب آدم وإبليس. «منها» أي من الجنة. وقد قال لإبليس: اخرج منها مذءوما مدحورا

QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r2.claim: Adam is hostile to the serpent and Iblis, while both are hostile to him; this rules out Adam and Eve as the two addressed, since they were not enemies, though Eve's descent is included in Adam's.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r2.anchor: وهذا يدل على أن قوله: «اهبطا» ليس خطابا لآدم وحواء لأنهما ما كانا متعاديين

QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r3.claim: Guidance here means right direction and true speech; Qurtubi says its explanation was given earlier in al-Baqara.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r3.anchor: أي رشدا وقولا حقا. وقد تقدم في «البقرة».

QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r4.claim: The guidance to be followed refers to the messengers and scriptures.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says God guarantees that whoever recites the Qur'an and acts on it will not stray in this world or suffer in the Hereafter, and he recited this verse.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس: ضمن الله تعالى لمن قرأ القرآن وعمل بما فيه ألا يضل في الدنيا، ولا يشقى في الآخرة

QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r6.claim: In another report, Ibn ʿAbbas says whoever reads and follows the Qur'an is guided from error and protected from a bad reckoning on Resurrection Day.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r6.anchor: وعنه: من قرأ القرآن واتبع ما فيه هداه الله من الضلالة، ووقاه يوم القيامة سوء الحساب، ثم تلا الآية

RAZI-FULL:v22p112/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p112/r1.speaker: أبو مسلم
RAZI-FULL:v22p112/r1.claim: Abū Muslim explains the dual descend as addressing Adam with his descendants and Iblīs with his descendants; each is a kind, so the dual fits, while each kind’s multitude explains the following plural you.
RAZI-FULL:v22p112/r1.anchor: قال أبو مسلم : الخطاب لآدم ومعه ذريته ولإبليس ومعه ذريته

RAZI-FULL:v22p112/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p112/r2.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v22p112/r2.claim: Al-Kashshāf explains that Adam and Eve are the source from whom humanity descended, so they are treated as humanity itself and addressed in the plural.
RAZI-FULL:v22p112/r2.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : لما كان آدم وحواء عليهما السلام أصلا للبشر

RAZI-FULL:v22p112/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p112/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p112/r3.claim: The plural address and promise of guidance indicate that the descendants of Adam are intended.
RAZI-FULL:v22p112/r3.anchor: فيه دلالة على أن المراد الذرية

RAZI-FULL:v22p112/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p112/r4.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v22p112/r4.claim: Al-Qāḍī says the wording is satisfied by Satan and devils being enemies to people and people being enemies to them; reciprocal enmity within each side may also be included.
RAZI-FULL:v22p112/r4.anchor: فقال القاضي : يكفي في توفية هذا الظاهر حقه

RAZI-FULL:v22p112/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p112/r5.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v22p112/r5.claim: Some identify the promised guidance as the messengers.
RAZI-FULL:v22p112/r5.anchor: وقد اختلفوا في المراد بالهدى ، فقال بعضهم : الرسل

RAZI-FULL:v22p112/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p112/r6.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v22p112/r6.claim: Others identify the promised guidance as proofs and indications, while another group identifies it as the Qurʾān.
RAZI-FULL:v22p112/r6.anchor: وبعضهم قال : الآخر والأدلة وبعضهم قال القرآن

RAZI-FULL:v22p112/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p112/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p112/r7.claim: Al-Rāzī’s synthesis is that guidance means indication broadly and therefore includes messengers, proofs, and the Qurʾān.
RAZI-FULL:v22p112/r7.anchor: والتحقيق أن الهدى عبارة عن الدلالة فيدخل فيه كل ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v22p112/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p112/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p112/r8.claim: Because the promise concerns following evidence, following must include both using the evidence to reason and acting on it; such a follower is promised neither error nor misery.
RAZI-FULL:v22p112/r8.anchor: واتباعها لا يتكامل إلا بأن يستدل بها وبأن يعمل بها

RAZI-FULL:v22p112/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p112/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p112/r9.claim: One reading is that the follower will not go astray in this world or suffer in the afterlife.
RAZI-FULL:v22p112/r9.anchor: لا يضل في الدنيا ولا يشقى في الآخرة

RAZI-FULL:v22p112/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p112/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p112/r10.claim: A second reading places both the absence of error and misery in the afterlife, where God guides the person to the Garden and enables him to dwell there.
RAZI-FULL:v22p112/r10.anchor: لا يضل ولا يشقى في الآخرة لأنه تعالى يهديه إلى الجنة ويمكنه فيها

RAZI-FULL:v22p112/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p112/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p112/r11.claim: A third reading places both promises in this world.
RAZI-FULL:v22p112/r11.anchor: لا يضل ولا يشقى في الدنيا

RAZI-FULL:v22p112/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p112/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p112/r12.claim: Although a follower of guidance may face worldly hardship, the promise means no religious error and no suffering caused by religion; hardship from another source is not excluded.
RAZI-FULL:v22p112/r12.anchor: المراد لا يضل في الدين ولا يشقى بسبب الدين فإن حصل الشقاء بسبب آخر فلا بأس

QUSHAYRI:v2p280/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p280/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p280/r9.claim: After the Fall, Adam and Eve faced enmity with Iblis and the serpent, separation from Paradise, worldly trials, and the desires of this life.
QUSHAYRI:v2p280/r9.anchor: توالت المحن على آدم وحواء بعد خروجهما من الجنة بسمة العصيان ، ومفارقة الجنة ، ودخول الدنيا

QUSHAYRI:v2p280/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p280/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p280/r10.claim: Whoever follows God's guidance, leaves personal desire, and refuses the enemy's whisper receives every good and no harm.
QUSHAYRI:v2p280/r10.anchor: وترك هواه ، ولم يعمل بوسوسة العدو فله كل خير ، ولا يلحقه ضير

STUDYQURAN:20:123/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:123/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:123/r1.claim: The address is understood to include Adam, Eve, and their future descendants, announcing their banishment from Paradise.
STUDYQURAN:20:123/r1.anchor: This verse is understood to be an address to Adam and Eve and their future progeny, indicating their banishment from Paradise

STUDYQURAN:20:123/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:123/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:123/r2.claim: Following God's guidance on earth is the means by which humanity can recover its original nature after the fall.
STUDYQURAN:20:123/r2.anchor: but also the means by which they could recover their original nature while on earth—by following God’s Guidance

TAB-FULL:v16p190#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p190#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p190#2/r1.claim: God commands Adam and Eve to descend to earth, then promises guidance to Adam, Eve, and Satan.
TAB-FULL:v16p190#2/r1.anchor: فإن يأتكم يا آدم وحواء وإبليس مني هدى

TAB-FULL:v16p190#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p190#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p190#2/r2.claim: Adam and Eve, and their descendants, are enemies of Satan and his descendants; Satan is their enemy.
TAB-FULL:v16p190#2/r2.anchor: فإن يأتكم يا آدم وحواء وإبليس مني هدى

TAB-FULL:v16p190#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p190#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p190#2/r3.claim: The guidance from God is clarification of His path and of the religion He chose for creation.
TAB-FULL:v16p190#2/r3.anchor: فإن يأتكم يا آدم وحواء وإبليس مني هدى: يقول: بيان لسبيلي، وما اختاره لخلقي من دين

TAB-FULL:v16p190#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p190#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p190#2/r4.claim: Following God's guidance means following that clarification, acting on it, and not deviating from it.
TAB-FULL:v16p190#2/r4.anchor: فمن اتبع بياني ذلك وعمل به، ولم يزغ منه

TAB-FULL:v16p190#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p190#2/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p190#2/r5.claim: The follower will not stray from the path of truth, but will be guided in this world.
TAB-FULL:v16p190#2/r5.anchor: فلا يزول عن محجة الحق، ولكنه يرشد في الدنيا ويهتدي

TAB-FULL:v16p190#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p190#2/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p190#2/r6.claim: The follower will not suffer punishment in the afterlife: God will admit him to Paradise and save him from torment.
TAB-FULL:v16p190#2/r6.anchor: في الآخرة بعقاب الله، لأن الله يدخله الجنة، وينجيه من عذابه

TAB-FULL:v16p190#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p190#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v16p190#2/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says God guarantees that whoever reads the Qur'an and follows its contents will not stray in this world or be miserable in the next.
TAB-FULL:v16p190#2/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: تضمن الله لمن قرأ القرآن، واتبع ما فيه أن لا يضل في الدنيا ولا يشقى في الآخرة

TAB-FULL:v16p190#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p190#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v16p190#2/r8.claim: In a report through Saʿid ibn Jubayr, Ibn Abbas says Qur'an-followers are protected from misguidance and perhaps from the terror of Resurrection; the transmitter marks the latter wording as uncertain.
TAB-FULL:v16p190#2/r8.anchor: عن عطاء، عن سعيد بن جبير، قال: قال ابن عباس: من قرأ القرآن واتبع ما فيه عصمه الله من الضلالة، ووقاه، أظنه أنه قال: من هول يوم القيامة

SULAMI:v1p453#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p453#2/r1.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v1p453#2/r1.claim: Following the path means adhering to the Book and Sunna; this keeps one from straying from guidance or suffering in this world and the next.
SULAMI:v1p453#2/r1.anchor: قال سهل : هو الإقتداء ، وملازمة الكتاب والسنة

TABATABAI:20:123/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:123/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:123/r1.claim: Guidance following divine selection concerns the religious felicity for which one is selected: exclusive servitude to God. This direct guidance never fails, unlike worldly benefits mediated by fallible causes.
TABATABAI:20:123/r1.anchor: ظاهر تفرع الهداية على الإجتباء كونه مهديا إلى ما كان الإجتباء له

TABATABAI:20:123/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:123/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:123/r2.claim: The descent and mutual enmity were explained earlier in the corresponding passages in al-Baqara and al-Aʿrāf.
TABATABAI:20:123/r2.anchor: تقدم تفسير مثله في سورتي البقرة والأعراف

TABATABAI:20:123/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:123/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:123/r3.claim: “He said” shifts from first-person plural to third-person singular; the shift may mark a decree and judgment, which belong to God alone.
TABATABAI:20:123/r3.anchor: ولعل الوجه فيه اشتمال الآية على القضاء والحكم وهو مما يختص به تعالى

TABATABAI:20:123/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:123/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:123/r4.claim: The construction derives from “if guidance comes to you,” augmented with mā and the emphatic nūn to signal that the condition will certainly occur.
TABATABAI:20:123/r4.anchor: زيد عليه ما ونون التأكيد للإشارة إلى وقوع الشرط

TABATABAI:20:123/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:123/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:123/r5.claim: “Follow My guidance” metaphorically makes the guidance the thing followed; the underlying sense is following the guide who guides by God's guidance.
TABATABAI:20:123/r5.anchor: نسبة الاتباع إلى الهدى على طريق الاستعارة بالكناية،

TABATABAI:20:123/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:123/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:123/r6.claim: The follower neither loses the way nor suffers in the outcome; the unrestricted promise covers both worldly and afterlife error and misery.
TABATABAI:20:123/r6.anchor: أي لا يضل في طريقه ولا يشقى في غايته التي هي عاقبة أمره

TABATABAI:20:123/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:123/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:123/r7.claim: Divine guidance is the natural religion: beliefs and acts called for by human nature and its endowment; each creature's happiness is what its created constitution requires.
TABATABAI:20:123/r7.anchor: ودين الفطرة هو مجموع الاعتقادات والأعمال التي تدعو إليها فطرة الإنسان وخلقته

TABATABAI:20:115-126#6/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:115-126#6/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:115-126#6/r1.claim: Reports applying “whoever follows My guidance” and “My remembrance” to the wilāya of the Prophet's household are instances of Qurʾānic application (jary), not lexical interpretation.
TABATABAI:20:115-126#6/r1.anchor: وقع فيها تطبيق قوله تعالى { فمن اتبع هداي } وقوله { عن ذكري } على ولاية أهل البيت

TABATABAI:20:115-126#6/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:115-126#6/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:20:115-126#6/r2.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās in al-Durr al-Manthūr says the Prophet promised that following God's Book guides one away from worldly error and protects one from an evil reckoning on Judgment Day.
TABATABAI:20:115-126#6/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:20:115-126#6/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:115-126#6/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:115-126#6/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī reads that report as assigning “does not stray” to worldly life and “is not miserable” to the afterlife, supporting his interpretation.
TABATABAI:20:115-126#6/r3.anchor: الحديث ينزل قوله تعالى { فلا يضل } على الدنيا وقوله { ولا يشقى } على الآخرة

TUSTARI:20:123/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:20:123/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:20:123/r1.claim: Following God's guidance means emulating the Prophet and keeping to the Book and Sunna, so one neither strays from guidance nor suffers in this life or the next.

TABRISI:20:124#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:124#2/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:124#2/r9.claim: The dual command to descend addresses Adam and Eve.
TABRISI:20:124#2/r9.anchor: قال اهبطا منها جميعا } يعني آدم وحواء

TABRISI:20:124#2/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:124#2/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:124#2/r10.claim: Following God’s guidance prevents error in this world and misery in the next.
TABRISI:20:124#2/r10.anchor: أي فلا يضل في الدنيا ولا يشقى في الآخرة

TABRISI:20:124#2/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:124#2/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:20:124#2/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas says God guarantees that anyone who reads the Qur’an and acts on it will not stray in this world or suffer in the next.
TABRISI:20:124#2/r11.anchor: قال ابن عباس: ضمن الله سبحانه لمن قرأ القرآن وعمل بما فيه أن لا يضل في الدنيا

THALABI:v6p264/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p264/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p264/r5.claim: The guidance God sends is the Book and the Messenger.
THALABI:v6p264/r5.anchor: فمن اتبع هداي يعني الكتاب والرسول فلا يضل ولا يشقى

THALABI:v6p264/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p264/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v6p264/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says God protects the follower of the Qur’an from worldly error and misery in the afterlife.
THALABI:v6p264/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله سبحانه فمن اتبع هداي فلا يضل ولا يشقى قال: أجار الله تعالى تابع القرآن

THALABI:v6p264/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p264/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v6p264/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says God guarantees that the Qur’an’s reciter will not stray in this life or suffer in the next.
THALABI:v6p264/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: ضمن الله لمن قرأ القرآن لا يضل في الدنيا ولا يشقى في الآخرة

THALABI:v6p264/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p264/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v6p264/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas says following the Qur’an guides a person from error and shields them from the bad reckoning on Judgment Day.
THALABI:v6p264/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: من قرأ القرآن واتبع ما فيه هداه الله من الضلالة ووقاه يوم القيامة سوء الحساب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p549#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p549#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p549#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the two commanded to descend as Adam and Iblīs.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p549#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p549#2/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p549#2/r2.claim: The author says this verse is explained in Sūrat al-Baqara, referring to the parallel account of Adam's descent and guidance.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p549#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p549#2/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p549#2/r3.claim: The author assigns “does not go astray” to this world and “does not suffer” to the next life.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p549#2/r3.anchor: {فلا يضل} أي: في الدنيا (ولا يشقى) [في الآخرة.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p549#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p549#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p549#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says God protects the follower of the Qurʾān from error in this world and misery in the next, quoting the verse.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p549#2/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (أجار الله تابع القرآن من أن يضل في الدنيا أو يشقى في الآخرة

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p285#2/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p285#2/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p285#2/r3.claim: The descent and enmity between them were explained earlier in Sūrat al-Baqarah.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p285#2/r3.anchor: {قال اهبطا منها جميعا بعضكم لبعض عدو} [طه: 123] وقد فسرناه في سورة البقرة.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p285#2/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p285#2/r4.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p285#2/r4.claim: Al-Suddi explains following God’s guidance as following His messengers and books.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p285#2/r4.anchor:
قوله: {فمن اتبع هداي} [طه: 123] يعني: رسلي وكتبي.
تفسير السدي.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p285#2/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p285#2/r5.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p285#2/r5.claim: The follower of guidance will not go astray in this world or be wretched in the hereafter.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p285#2/r5.anchor:
{فلا يضل} [طه: 123] في الدنيا.
{ولا يشقى} [طه: 123] في الآخرة.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r2.claim: Earlier passages in Ṣād and al-Aʿrāf recount Adam, Iblis’s disobedience, the couple’s conditional stay in the garden, Satan’s enticement and their expulsion; retelling these matters in different contexts and styles is characteristic of the Qur’an.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r2.anchor: Yine A‘râf sûresinde Âdem’e –yasak ağaca yaklaşmamaları koşuluyla– eşiyle birlikte cennette kalma imkânı verildiğinden

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p370#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p370#2/r5.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p370#2/r5.claim: The first Qurʾanic sense of shaqāʾ is toil, including the statements that the Prophet was not burdened with the Qurʾan and the follower will not suffer.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p370#2/r5.anchor: أحدها : التعب . ومنه قوله تعالى ( في سورة طه )

BURHAN:v1p115/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p115/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p115/r4.claim: Ta-Ha uses اتبع instead of تبع to match its later wording يتبعون الداعي.
